text:
Maya (CS): FYI customer Acme opened a ticket — big invoice spike this month, says billed tokens >> served tokens. They point at times when their traffic is steady but our billed column jumps. Can we triage?

Acme Support (customer): See invoice lines for 2026-02-12 02:00-04:00 UTC. We didn't change traffic. We see a billed_tokens = 3.2M vs served_tokens = 1.1M. Request ids: r-11a2, r-11a3.

Maya (CS): Thanks — passing to runtime and billing. @Arun can you look at batcher/prefetch logs for those request ids?

Arun (Eng): grabbing logs now. quick note: customer uses continuous_batcher + kv_prefix_cache + prefetch enabled. That stack is where we've seen odd accounting before.

Evan (SRE): I pulled traces for r-11a2. Observed these headers in ingress trace: 
```
X-Redwood-Served-Tokens: 1142
X-Redwood-Billed-Tokens: 3320
X-Redwood-Trace: r-11a2
X-Redwood-Batcher: inflight-window=50ms,coalesce=15ms
```

Arun (Eng): Interesting — the billed tokens match what the batcher emitted after coalescing, not the per-request served tokens post-kv-hit. Looks like we attribute entire batch output to each request in some accounting path.

Maya (CS): Is that intended? Customer expects billed ~= served when cache hits happen.

Arun (Eng): No, not intended. For continuous_batcher we route through batch accounting which currently records billed tokens at the batch level, then splits by request in a best-effort way. If a request had a KV prefix hit that short-circuited generation, we don't always subtract the saved tokens correctly for that request. Edgecase: warm prefetch can cause the batch to be populated but later resolved by KV hits before actual decode.

Sylvia (Billing): Are we sure invoice numbers are coming from the same accounting pipeline as the per-request metric user sees in dashboard? There are two places: realtime-metering (dashboard) and billing-aggregator (invoice pipeline). They should converge but batching makes it hard.

Arun (Eng): Correct. Dashboard uses served-token events emitted at request completion. Billing aggregator consumes batch-issued events earlier in the pipeline (batch emission + router attribution). There's a window where a prefetch cancel or kv-hit later reduces served tokens but the batch-level event already pushed billed tokens upstream.

Acme Support (customer): So we were charged for tokens that our client never actually paid compute for? That's a big deal.

Evan (SRE): Practically: we charged for capacity used when the batch expanded. Even if some requests turned into KV hits later, the batch had reserved GPU cycles. Billing policy we implemented charges on batch emission to keep accounting consistent with capacity allocation. But we need to make this explicit to customers.

Maya (CS): Can we provide a repro and mitigation? Customer asked for a reconciled invoice or credit while we root-cause.

Arun (Eng): Repro steps I'm using locally:
1) Start model with continuous_batcher enabled: --batcher=continuous --coalesce-ms=15 --inflight-window-ms=50
2) Enable kv_prefix_cache + prefetch (prefetch TTL short)
3) Send controlled workload: 20 concurrent short prefix-only requests that would hit kv cache if prefetch completes. Use this script:
```
for i in {1..20}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"prefix-only-${i}","max_tokens":256}' &
done; wait
```
4) Observe metrics: batcher logs show batch_size spikes and batch_billed_tokens ~= sum(decoded tokens). Per-request served tokens (from completed requests) show many zeros due to KV hits.

Arun (Eng): Quick log snippet for a repro run: 
```
[2026-02-12T02:12:23Z] batcher: created batch id=b-901 size=18 estimated_tokens=3240
[2026-02-12T02:12:23Z] prefetch: enqueued prefetch for pfx=\"usr:acct:abc\" reqs=18
[2026-02-12T02:12:23Z] kv_cache: hit 12/18 -> short-circuit responses
[2026-02-12T02:12:23Z] batcher: emitted billed_event batch=b-901 billed_tokens=3240
[2026-02-12T02:12:23Z] router: attribute billed_event -> per-request attribution (best-effort)
[2026-02-12T02:12:23Z] request r-xyz served_tokens=0
```

Sylvia (Billing): If billing-aggregator received the billed_event then invoice shows the 3240 tokens. Dashboard shows served_tokens sum = 6*estimated -> discrepancy. We'll need to reconcile for the invoice.

Evan (SRE): Short-term mitigation: disable prefetch for the customer or reduce coalesce/inflight window so batcher emits less aggressive batches. That reduces the window where billed_event and final served state diverge.

Maya (CS): Can we propose a credit for the delta while we fix attribution?

Sylvia (Billing): I'll flag BILL-2348 (internal) and suggest a one-time invoice credit for the reconciled delta for Feb 12 window if we confirm repro. We need engineering sign-off for root cause and a patch plan.

Arun (Eng): Action items:
- I will run controlled repro on prod-like cluster and capture exact events (batch emission, kv-hit, serve completion).
- Evan to check whether billing-aggregator can be modified to listen for final served tokens and backfill/correct billed attribution when KV short-circuit occurs.
- Maya to update customer with repro ETA and offer mitigations (turn off prefetch or tweak batcher).

Maya (CS): Customer prefers we do mitigations first. Offering to toggle prefetch now — @Acme Support do you want us to toggle off prefetch while we investigate?

Acme Support (customer): Yes please toggle off. Also requesting an interim credit while this is investigated.

Sylvia (Billing): Toggled prefetch off for Acme on staging and will schedule change on their prod account after-hours if CS approves. Opening invoice credit request in BILL-2348.

Arun (Eng): Follow-up: initial repro shows the attribution bug in router attribution component when batch-level billed_event is emitted before request completion. Proposed long-term fix: change billing-aggregator to accept a tombstone/correction event from request completion that adjusts billed attribution (idempotent). Short term: make batcher emit a per-request provisional billed event with a flag that allows later reconciliation.

Evan (SRE): Logging checklist before we close: capture batch_id, per-request reason (kv-hit/prefetch/normal), timestamps for batch emit and request completion, and correlation ids. Also add metric: billed_vs_served_delta per account.

Maya (CS): Thanks all. I'll update Acme with mitigation timeline and link to BILL-2348. :thumbsup:

BillingBot: Ticket BILL-2348 created and assigned to @Sylvia (Billing). Priority: P2.

Arun (Eng): I'll post repro artifacts and a small demo script here when done.

Maya (CS): Marking follow-up for tomorrow morning. :eyes:
